(i) use of the SimpleX search in side-chain identification and fitting can improve the average amino-acid selection by over 2.5-fold (from 25 to 32%); (ii) use of the sequence alignment to correct errors in side-chain identification can improve the average selection by over 3-fold (from 32 to 77%); and (iii) the combined use of the Simple-X search and sequence alignment to correct the side-chain identification can further improve the selection

the use of the Nelder-Mead simplex search for side-chain selection can improve the accuracy of the side-chain identification, and that the use of a sequence alignment in combination with the Nelder-Meed simplex search improves the amino-acid selection by an additional 13 percentage points.

(a) the Simplex search method is an effective tool for improving the accuracy of amino-acid selection and side-chain fitting in automated protein model building, (b) this is especially true when coupled with sequence-alignment correction of side-chain identification errors and (c) the Simplex method is particularly effective for improving side-chain identification and fitting when the backbone is not accurately modeled.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a Nelder-Meed Simplex search in TEXTAL improves the accuracy of side-chain identification and fitting, and that this improvement can be exploited by using sequence alignment to improve the overall side-chain identification accuracy.

the use of Simplex search in the identification of amino-acid residues and the fitting of their models can improve the accuracy of automated model building in X ray crystallography, and that the improvements are sufficient to allow the use of automated methods for model building in cases in which sequence alignment would otherwise be required.
the use of the SimpleX search in TEXTAL, coupled with sequence alignment when appropriate, can significantly improve the accuracy of side-chain identification and C(alpha) predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the Simple x search in TEXTAL improved side-chain identification and fit by an average of 7% over the previous version.

use of the SimpleX search in TEXTAL improves amino-acid identification and fit by 10-25%, and when combined with sequence alignment it improves amino-acid selection and fit by 13-38% over using sequence alignment alone.

the use of the Nelder-Mead search in TEXTAL improves the initial amino-acid sidechain selection by over 13% on average (without sequence alignment) and by over 25 percentage points (on average) when coupled with sequence alignment.

the accuracy of side-chain identification and fit can be improved by using the Simplex search in the model-building process.
